newsitem.title: INDIA: CRISIL gives A+ rating for India JK bond.
newsitem.headline: CRISIL gives A+ rating for India JK bond.

text.p: The Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said it assigned a A+ rating to J.K. Industries Ltd's (JKIL) 400 million rupees non-convertible debenture (NCD) issue.
The rating indicates adequate safety on timely payment of interest and principal, it said in a statement.
JKIL is in the business of manufacture and sale of tyres which constitutes around 85-90 percent of the company's gross sales turnover and bulk of its profitability, CRISIL said.
Besides tyres, the company has diversified into sugar, pharmaceuticals and agri-genetics.
Over the years, JKIL has built up a competitive market position in the truck tyre segment and is well placed in the growing market for radial tyres for passenger cars and LCVs.

While the company has been able to maintain its position as a significant player in the tyre industry, there has been a gradual decline in its profitability, as reflected in the financial performance for the period 1992-93 to 1994-95.

Though the operating income of the company has increased from 4,234.8 million rupees in 1992-93 to 6,310.3 million rupees in 1994-95, the operating margins (OPBDIT/Operating income) of the company have declined from 15.7 percent in 1992-93 to 10.4 percent in 1994-95 on account of increased competition and substantial increase in rubber prices in line with the trends witnessed by the industry.
The company's operations during the year 1995-96 were affected by labour problems which may result in a further drop in the company's margins in the tyre business this year.

JKIL's future plans in this business include expanding existing capacities, likely acquisition of controlling stake in Vikrant Tyres and a proposed joint venture with an international major, CRISIL said.
It said the oversupply situation in the tyre industry is expected to continue in the future due to likely additions in capacities which would in turn impact JKIL's performance.
However, in short to medium term, the company's passenger radial expansion, where there is a strong growth in demand, would place it in a relatively comfortable position.
With JKIL undertaking expansion/modernisation programmes, its ability to implement various projects in a timely manner will impact its future cash flows, it said.
